deadline: Saturday before sprint race start (12:00 PM local / 5:00 PM UK)
central_unknown: Mercedes and McLaren are both bringing upgrade packages to Canada, and it's unclear which team will emerge stronger — this determines whether the optimal constructor pairing is Mercedes+Ferrari or McLaren+Ferrari (or even Mercedes+McLaren for high-budget teams).

budget_tiers.core: Antonelli (2x), Mercedes or Ferrari constructor, second top constructor, Ocon/Colapinto
budget_tiers.fills: Pérez, Bortoleto or Bottas as budget fillers
Double Cadillac (Pérez + Bottas), Albon or Colapinto

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: Championship leader, safest price target at -4 points to avoid drop, Mercedes historically dominant at Montreal with upgrades incoming, won the race last year.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: George Russell
captains.reason: Back-to-back podiums in Canada, won 2025 Canadian GP, scored his highest fantasy total of last season here (47 pts). Suggested by 2024 Global League winner Andrew as a sneaky 2x differential. Mercedes bringing big upgrade package. Needs 34 pts for price gain but has scored 40+ in both sprint weekends this season.

buy.name: Sergio Pérez
buy.note: Lowest price rise target alongside Alonso. Scored 39 fantasy points across first two sprint weekends from 26 overtakes (5th on grid). Needs only -2 points to avoid price fall, 5 points for max rise. Strong budget builder for sprint weekends.

buy.name: Esteban Ocon
buy.note: P2 in season overtakes, scored championship points in all 6 career Canadian GP starts. Must-have midfield driver per FanAmp. Consistent scorer.

buy.name: Franco Colapinto
buy.note: Alpine showed strong pace in Miami (outperformed Williams). Good sprint weekend upside in a faster car than Sainz/Williams.

buy.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
buy.note: Cheapest viable sub-6M option after Bottas. 5 points to avoid price fall, 9 for max rise. Three positive-point races in four starts. Audi reliability is the risk — both drivers have finished together only once.

buy.name: Valtteri Bottas
buy.note: Near price floor (can only lose 0.9M more). Stop-loss budget filler. Hasn't scored 5+ points in any race this year though — pure budget placeholder if you need to free up funds for constructors.

consider.name: Fernando Alonso
consider.note: Low price rise target (-2 to avoid fall, 5 for max gain). Finished top 10 in Canada each of last 4 seasons. However, Aston Martin brought no upgrades in Miami and reliability is a concern — 8 DNFs in 20 Canadian GP starts. FanAmp prefers Pérez and Colapinto at similar prices.

consider.name: Alex Albon
consider.note: Needs 7 points to avoid price fall, 16 for max rise — in the 'need some luck' category. Was among top 5 budget scorers in Miami but unclear if Williams pace holds.

avoid: Nico Hulkenberg — heading toward 3M price floor after DNS in sprint and DNF in race at Miami, Audi reliability catastrophic
Liam Lawson — DNF'd in Miami, needs 24 points to avoid price drop which is a big ask
Ollie Bearman — only 6 points in Miami after crash in Japan, needs 34 points to avoid price drop, likely a sell in Canada
Arvid Lindblad — DNF'd in Miami, sell candidate
Pierre Gasly — sell column per multiple sources
Lance Stroll — still carrying negative points from Japan, needs 16 points to avoid further price fall

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: Multiple sources considering wildcard for Canada if teams are in bad shape from Miami DNFs/price drops (Hulkenberg, Lawson, Bearman all falling). FormulaFantasyHub specifically has wildcard 'very seriously on the table' for his underperforming team. Good opportunity to pivot into budget builders like Pérez, Alonso, Bortoleto and lock in two top constructors.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: Consensus leans toward saving Limitless for Monaco rather than Canada. Canada historically 21st in overtakes (low scoring). Monaco's track position emphasis and Ferrari's strong starts could make it higher value. However, if weather disrupts the race, any chip played risks being wasted.

chips.name: No Negative
chips.reason: Rain threat has diminished significantly for Canada (was high earlier in the week, now mostly dry forecast). ReinFantasy noted that if thunderstorms cause a shortened race, the chip loses value. Better saved for a confirmed wet/chaotic weekend.

watch_items: Mercedes upgrade package debut in Canada — Toto Wolff confirmed first major upgrade of the season; could restore early-season dominance
McLaren upgrade continuation — next phase of their package arriving at Canada after strong Miami showing
Weather still volatile — was forecasting rain Saturday/Sunday earlier in the week but has since cleared; could shift back closer to race day
First ever sprint race weekend at Canadian Grand Prix — only 60-minute FP1 before sprint qualifying, limited setup time
Audi/Cadillac reliability — both teams have had both drivers finish together only once this season; critical for anyone running Bortoleto or Pérez
George Russell's Canada form — back-to-back podiums, won in 2025, historically strong here; could outperform Antonelli
Esteban Ocon's Canada record — scored points in all 6 career races here
arc: Canada is a pivotal budget-rebuilding week after Miami's carnage of DNFs and price drops decimated many managers' squads. The sprint format offers extra scoring potential but also extra risk. The key strategic tension is whether to play the Limitless chip here or hold it for Monaco (consensus favors Monaco). Mercedes and McLaren upgrades debuting in Canada will reshape the constructor hierarchy — if Mercedes reasserts dominance with their upgrade and Russell/Antonelli lock out the front row, Mercedes becomes the must-own constructor through Monaco. If McLaren's upgrades work better, the meta could shift to McLaren+Ferrari. Budget drivers like Pérez, Bortoleto, and Bottas need to be locked in now as holds through Monaco, where many managers plan to deploy Limitless. The back-to-back racing resumes after Canada with Monaco and then a run of races, so getting your squad structure right here sets the foundation for the next month.
